rows.grounds: kaṭākṣa (sidelong glance) in instrumental singular fused with emphatic particle eva; denotes the sole means
refers back to the effects listed in the preceding verses (drāvaṇa, bhīṣaṇa, etc.)
genitive indicating the agent for whom the accomplishments occur
conjunction ca with adverb anyathā, reinforcing exclusion of any other way

items.question: What sole means enables the practitioner to accomplish all these effects?
premises: The excellent practitioner accomplishes various powerful effects.
All these effects are accomplished by a sidelong glance alone.
No other means brings about these accomplishments for the practitioner.
items.inference: Therefore the practitioner's sidelong glance alone suffices for all these accomplishments.
uncertainties: sarvāṇi is understood to refer to the effects enumerated in verses 23–24.
items.plain_english: For the practitioner, all these are accomplished by a mere sidelong glance alone, and not otherwise.
